title: Rate-cap bridge + hedged fallback for cross-region limiter continuity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a cross-region fallback mechanism that preserves SLOs and fairness when a regional quota controller is degraded or partitioned. Current behavior: regional limiter outages or high latency cause either hard-deny (client errors) or aggressive local shedding that results in unfair token loss and poor UX for multi-region customers.

Goal:
Implement a "rate-cap bridge" with hedged request fallback and short-lived token borrowing to provide graceful continuity during limiter outages or high-latency windows. The bridge should: (1) allow transient burst absorption without violating global SLO targets, (2) maintain per-customer fairness, and (3) provide clear observability and rollback controls.

Background and motivation:
- We observe repeated incidents where a region's limiter control-plane (lease store or coordinator) experiences high tail latency; callers either see 429s or client-side retries that increase load elsewhere.
- Multi-region customers expect consistent throughput across failovers; simple local over-allowance breaks cost accounting and SLA guarantees.
- Existing mitigation (hard circuit-breakers or static fallbacks) are too coarse: either too permissive (blow budget) or too strict (drop important traffic).

Proposed design (high level):
1) Short-lived bridge tokens: when a regional limiter cannot confirm a token within X ms, the edge will issue a short-lived bridge token (TTL 2s) that permits the request to proceed. These tokens are accounted and reconciled asynchronously with a global lease reconciler.
2) Hedged fallback requests: for critical routes, clients will issue a hedged read to a secondary region after Y ms; the first successful response wins. The bridge logic prevents double-counting by marking hedged attempts with the bridge token id.
3) Soft global caps + borrower pool: create a global soft cap per-customer (a small percentage above guaranteed regional capacity) that funds short-term borrowing. Borrowed capacity must be repaid by reducing allowance in subsequent windows or drained from a background reconciliation job.
4) Deterministic fairness algorithm: when multiple regions use bridge tokens concurrently, enforce per-customer weighted deficit accounting so the borrower pool is distributed according to configured weights (customer tier + route priority).
5) Circuit-breaker tiers: three modes (Normal, Bridge-enabled, Hard-isolate). On control-plane degradation, transition to Bridge-enabled, then to Hard-isolate if backend errors or reconciliation fails for >T_fail. Escalation thresholds are configurable per-region.
6) Observability and rollback: expose metrics (bridge_token_issued, bridge_token_reconciled, borrow_pool_utilization, hedged_win_rate) and a console route to revoke bridge issuance for a region immediately.

Acceptance criteria:
- No increase in 95th percentile end-to-end latency beyond SLO for normal traffic when bridge is exercised in a controlled test (simulated 30s coordinator latency in region us-west-2).
- Fairness preserved: in k-sim tests with mixed-tenancy traffic, per-customer throughput deviation vs baseline <= 10% after 1 minute stabilization.
- Auditability: every bridge token must be reconcilable to a lease record within 60s during reconciliation run; unreconciled tokens trigger alert.
- Fail-safe: if global borrower pool exceeds 80% utilization, system shifts to Hard-isolate within 10s and emits an incident annotation.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike (2w): prototype bridge token format, lightweight reconciler, and hedged-client simulation harness. (Aisha, Marcel)
- Core feature (3w): edge issuance path, per-customer borrow accounting, and deterministic fairness algorithm + unit tests. (Marcel, Daniel)
- Reconciler + control plane integration (2w): background drain job, console toggles, and alerting. (Infra team: Lina)
- Load test & chaos (1w): multi-region load tests with simulated coordinator latency and network partitions. Create test harness runbook. (SRE)
- Gradual rollout (2w): canary in non-critical customers, staged to paid tiers. Monitor metrics and define rollback criteria.

Rollout plan and safety knobs:
- Start in Bridge-enabled read-only mode (issue tokens but reduce borrow_pool to 5% of sum capacity) in canary region.
- Provide console kill-switch to disable bridge issuance per-region.
- Auto-escalation to Hard-isolate if reconciler lag > 60s or borrow_pool_utilization > 80%.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for token issuance and reconciliation logic.
- Deterministic integration tests across 3 simulated regions.
- K-sim fairness bench comparing baseline and bridge-enabled scenarios with contention mix (40% p99-chattiness clients, 60% steady traffic).
- Post-mortem injection test: run fault-injection for 5m and validate automated rollback triggers.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Token TTL sizing: short TTL reduces double-spend risk but increases chance of conservative denial; propose 2s as starting point but tunable per route.
- Accounting window for repayment: immediate negative adjustment vs amortized over 1 minute; prefer amortized to avoid sharp throttles.
- Cost visibility: bridge tokens complicate per-request cost attribution; need billing team input for final strategy.

References and artifacts:
- PoC repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rlimit-bridge/pull/12
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Rate+Cap+Bridge+Design
- Load dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/limiter/bridge-experiments
- Related tickets: ENG-46210 (weighted donation prefetch leases), ENG-52377 (progressive fair-share smoothing)
comments: 2026-02-02 - Marcel Nguyen: Spike started. Implemented prototype bridge token serialization and a tiny in-memory reconciler. Observed reconciliation loop can catch up within 20s under moderate load.
2026-02-10 - SRE review (Lina): Concern about reconciler state explosion; suggested sharding by customer id hash and using GRPC streaming for reconciler input to avoid bursts.
2026-02-17 - Product (Ravi Shah): Approved project direction; requested billing impact analysis and a per-customer alerting signal for unexpected borrow usage.
2026-02-25 - Daniel Ortiz (Eng): Implemented deterministic fairness algorithm using token deficit buckets. Benchmarks: deviation reduced to ~6% in synthetic multi-tenant run.
2026-03-03 - Marcel: Added console feature flag and per-region kill-switch. Began canary in staging for non-critical routes (canary id: BRG-CAN-03).

2026-03-08 - QA: Found race where hedged requests cause duplicate accounting when both succeed within TTL; mitigation: include bridge_token_id in response path and make reconciler idempotent. Added integration test.
2026-03-10 - Aisha: Next steps - finalize PR for reconciler sharding, add billing team to review, schedule chaos test on 2026-03-15.
